tier_reason: The only rasterizer claim is one README sentence (line 29) saying the library is 'at least twice as fast as existing solutions' and handles bigger images than Inkscape and Cairo for an extreme case, pointing at issue #280 comment 1995990038; that comment does not render in WebFetch (three tries, comments are loaded client-side), and no benchmark code, timing table, machine or harness for rasterization exists in the repo (renderers/rasterizer holds only rasterizer.go and util.go, no *_test.go benchmarks) or in tdewolff/canvas_benchmarks, which covers only polygon boolean operations. A directional claim with no verifiable number is tier D.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (directional, no number on the page): 'Execution performance is actually really good, especially the rasterizer is highly optimized with ASM. See for example a comparison of an extreme case in issue #280 (comment 1995990038), where this library is at least twice as fast as existing solutions, and can handle bigger images than the likes of Inkscape and Cairo.' The linked comment could not be read, so no timing, ratio or image size is verified.
corrections.baseline: Inkscape and Cairo (named in the README as 'existing solutions'; which Cairo-based tool was run, e.g. rsvg-convert or CairoSVG, is not stated on any readable page)
corrections.workload: End-to-end conversion of one very large SVG (score.svg attached to issue #280, a bug report about a pathIntersections panic) to a raster image; this includes SVG parsing, path processing and rasterization, so it is not a rasterizer-only comparison with Cairo. The comparison comment itself could not be read.
corrections.caveats: No numbers verifiable: the README links a single issue comment (issue #280, comment 1995990038, March 2024) that does not render outside a browser; no benchmark code, hardware, Go version or command lines for the rasterization comparison are public in the repo. One extreme-case file only; the issue's own opening post says canvas 'takes ages' on that file while JSVG (Java) takes 'a second or two', i.e. before the fixes canvas was slower than another renderer. The README's 'highly optimized with ASM' wording describes the golang.org/x/image/vector backend in use in March 2024 (whose accumulation loop has amd64 assembly); since commit 'Use Scanx rasterizer, fixes #334' (2025-02-06) the default renderers/rasterizer path uses the pure-Go srwiley/scanx scanner (rasterizer.go even carries a TODO to add an ASM version), after issue #334 reported x/image/vector as 500-1000x slower than scanx for GUI rounded-rectangle workloads. So the 2x claim, if it was ever measured, was measured on a superseded backend. The separate tdewolff/canvas_benchmarks repo covers polygon boolean operations only (canvas is slower than iOverlay there and comparable to Clipper2), not rasterization. First-party, no methodology. The code is MIT, but the README warns that FriBidi (used for text bidirectionality) is LGPL. Language is Go.

notes: Downgraded C to D: the claim exists only as a README sentence pointing at an unreadable issue comment, with no number, machine or harness anywhere reachable. Notable (1.8k stars, active, last commit 2026-09-23), so kept rather than rejected; language Go, MIT, copyable. Worth a retier only if someone can read issue #280 comment 1995990038 from an environment that renders GitHub comments.
